# 2002A Question 14 {.unnumbered}

::: {.exam-question}
## Question {.question-label}

[**Briefly outline**]{.task-verb} pharmacological methods of reducing gastric acidity. [**Indicate**]{.task-verb} the mechanisms of action and the advantages and disadvantages of each method.
:::

Also asked in: [2005A Question 6](/content/exams/anzca/2005/A/6/index.qmd#examiner-comments)

:::: {#answer-structure}

## Suggested Structure

[**Briefly outline**]{.task-verb} the methods in a comparison table. [**Indicate**]{.task-verb} the mechanism, advantages and disadvantages of each, including their perioperative relevance.

::: {.structure-table}
| Feature | Mechanism | Advantages | Disadvantages |
|---|---|---|---|
| Antacids | | | |
| Histamine-2 Antagonists | | | |
| Proton Pump Inhibitors | | | |
| Prostaglandin Analogues | | | |
| Anticholinergic Agents | | | |
:::

::::

## Examiner Comments

::: {.examiner-comments}
There was a **59%** pass rate for this question. Good answers included discussion of antacids (non-particulate and particulate), histamine-2 antagonists, proton pump inhibitors, prostaglandin analogues (misoprostol) and anticholinergic agents. Areas that were often inadequately discussed were antacids, perioperative reduction of acidity and advantages/disadvantages of the methods outlined.
:::
